scenes.line1: How does Kafka keep your data safe?
scenes.say: How does Kafka keep your data safe and scale with your needs? Let’s break down the basics.

scenes.label: Topic
scenes.sub: A topic is a named stream, split into partitions.
scenes.say: A topic is just a named stream of records. Each topic gets split into partitions for better performance.
Each partition is an ordered, unchangeable list of records. Every record has a unique offset. Brokers are the servers that store these partitions.
Replication copies partitions across brokers. If one goes down, your data stays safe and available.

scenes.question: Is an offset unique across all topics?
scenes.right: No, offsets are unique only within a partition.
scenes.say: Watch out: offsets are unique only within each partition, not across the whole system.
